newsitem.title: NORWAY: SPEEDSKATING-GERMANY'S SCHENK DOMINATES WOMEN'S EVENT.
newsitem.headline: SPEEDSKATING-GERMANY'S SCHENK DOMINATES WOMEN'S EVENT.

text.p: Germany's Franziska Schenk dominated the World sprint speedskating championship at the weekend, winning all four races in the women's competition.
Schenk, 22, piled up 159.090 points to capture gold ahead of Chinese rival Xue Ruihong with 160.985 points. Christine Witty of the United States won bronze with 161.495 points.
Schenk triumphed in both heats of the 500 and 1,000 metre distance on Saturday and Sunday in the Olympic Viking Ship arena in Hamar, north of Oslo.

Russian Sergei Klevchenya, who won Saturday's 500 metres race, captured gold in the men's event with 146.215 points. Norway's Roger Stroem ending in second place with 146.420 points while Casey FitzRandolph of the United States gathered 146.510 points for a bronze medal.
Japan's Manabu Horii swept the other three races in the men's competition but ruined his chances by falling in the race won by Klevchenya. Horii finished in 33rd place in the total standings.
